title: Which errors does practice remove?
hook: Two toy practice policies repeat four rounds, but only one corrects identified errors.

knows: basic arithmetic and how to compare two stated rules
doesNotKnow: how to distinguish time spent repeating from specified error correction, while keeping correction success an assumption

misconception: Repeating the same performance necessarily removes errors even without a mechanism that changes them.
objective: Distinguish time spent repeating from specified error correction, while keeping correction success an assumption.

claims.text: Peak; Anders Ericsson and Robert Pool; 2016.
claims.source: Candidate bibliographic record for peak-feedback-2016; edition and original publication year require independent authoritative checking. No book source was opened by this drafter.

claims.text: Peak emphasizes targeted practice with informative feedback rather than repetition alone.
claims.source: Peak (2016), candidate original-language edition; relevant chapter/section unconfirmed, not supplied or fabricated. Proposed attribution in our own words; fact-checker must open the book before publication.

claims.text: Original stipulated toy: Error inventory fixed; correction succeeds exactly as stipulated; no new errors, forgetting, transfer or empirical practice curve. Exact feedback inputs [{"label": "Repeat unchanged", "values": [8, 0, 0, 4]}, {"label": "Correct one/round", "values": [8, 0, 1, 4]}]; second author arithmetic check A=8, B=4. Repeating unchanged leaves {A}; correcting one per round leaves {B}. Only the specified correction operation removes errors.
